title: Affine-line purity
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), let $Y$ be the scheme of the
affine-line datum and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ with $\Lambda=A$. The affine-line purity
comparison $\gamma_{p,K}$ of
[def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison] – the adjoint of the
projection-formula composite
$Rp_!Lp^*K(1)[2]\cong K\otimes^L Rp_!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]\to K$
formed with the projective-line trace and normalized by the orientation
$\operatorname{pur}_s$ of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] – is an isomorphism

$$
\gamma_{p,K}:Lp^*K(1)[2]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp^!K.
$$

It is natural in $K$ and compatible with arbitrary base change of $Y$.
(Source: the relative affine-line case of cohomological purity, as in
Milne, Lectures on Etale Cohomology, Section 16, Theorems 16.1 and
16.7 and Proposition 16.11, with the acyclicity computation of Example
16.3 and the Gysin sequence of the divisor, over an arbitrary base
scheme.)

On the ordinary etale site, [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction] constructs $Rp_!\dashv p^*(1)[2]$ by composing $j_!\da

proof.text: Put $X=\mathbf A^1_Y$, $P=\mathbf P^1_Y$, and write $a:X\hookrightarrow P$ for the compactifying open immersion (distinct from the punctured-line immersion in the affine-line datum), so $p=qa$. The standard open immersion and properness of $q$ are [lemma-nagata-relative-affine-space-open-immersion] and [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], so this really is a compactification. The quasi-compactness required of the open follows once $P$ is Noetherian. The hypotheses of [def-pur-affine-line-datum] include $Y$ separated finite type over $k$, $A=A_{E,n}$, $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$, and $\ell\ne p_{\mathrm{char}}$. Hence $Y,X,P$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied over the spectrum of the field and then to the polynomial charts. Put $r=n/e$ and $m=\ell^r$, so $mA=0$ and $m$ is invertible on all these schemes. The specified pro-etale twist agrees with the realization of the ordinary etale twist $\mu_m\otimes_{\mathbf Z/m}A$ by [lem-pur-finite-kummer-level]; it is locally free of rank one by [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free]. Its ordinary-etale representative is locally constant and free of rank one by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. Choose a bounded constructible ordinary-etale representative $K_0$ and $\alpha:\nu_Y^*K_0\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ using [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Its finite Tor amplitude is that of $K$, by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude]. The same applies after pullback along $p,q,a$: [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] gives finite Tor amplitude and constructibility on the pro-etale site, and the origin and Tor-comparison statements give the corresponding properties on the etale representatives. Tensoring with the locally free rank-one twist is exact locally and only shifts the cohomological and Tor intervals by $[2]$. No preservation theorem for $Rp^!$ is being assumed. Applied to $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound] supplies a finite integer $d$ bounding $\dim P$ (the unique fibre is $P$); this verifies the compactification-dimension hypothesis of the actual-adjoint comparison used in Step 5. The same argument applies over any base $Y'$ in the chapter setting.

source.place: Proof, coefficient comparison sentence: verify finite etale-origin, Tor and dimension hypotheses

proof.text:
Work first on the ordinary etale sites, where inverse image for constant coefficients is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so $Lp^*=p^*$ and $Lq^*=q^*$. Set $T_P=A_P(1)[2]$, $T_X=a^*T_P$, $G_q(L)=q^*L\otimes_A^LT_P$, and $G_p(L)=a^*G_q(L)=p^*L(1)[2]$. By [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], $Rq_*\dashv G_q$ with actual counit $\epsilon_{q,L}=(1_L\otimes t_q)\pi_q^{-1}$. By [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], $Da_!\dashv a^*$ on the entire ordinary derived categories; denote its evaluation counit by $e_a$. The compactification formula [def-amb-etale-compact-support] gives $F_p=Rq_*Da_!$. Compose these two adjunctions using [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. It gives $F_p\dashv G_p$ with actual counit
$$\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p,L}=\epsilon_{q,L}\circ Rq_*(e_{a,G_qL}):Rq_*Da_!a^*G_qL\longrightarrow L.$$
Thus the adjunction includes its counit, not just the existence of a right adjoint.

source.place: Proof, first sentence: compose the open and normalized projective-line adjunctions

proof.text:
Identify this counit at $L=K_0$. Let $u:Da_!T_X\to T_P$ be $e_{a,T_P}$ and put $\int_p=t_q\circ Rq_*u$. Write $\rho:Da_!a^*(q^*K_0\otimes^LT_P)\xrightarrow{\sim}q^*K_0\otimes^LDa_!T_X$ for the inverse open projection map, with the tensor symmetry understood. Its invertibility is the case $f=a$ of [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]; the same node for $f=p$ gives the compact-support projection isomorphism. The open evaluation satisfies
$$e_{a,q^*K_0\otimes T_P}=(1_{q^*K_0}\otimes u)\rho.$$
Indeed the counit of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] is identity on every etale test object factoring through $X$; on such an object the displayed equation sends $x\otimes t$ to $x\otimes t$, and on the zero-extension presheaf's other components both maps are zero. Choose K-flat representatives with flat terms using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. The same equality holds in each bidegree of their tensor complexes, and the maps respect the tensor differentials, so it gives the asserted equality for derived tensor. No equality of unspecified isomorphisms is being assumed. By the compactification definition of the projection map [def-exchange-projection], its inverse at $T_X,K_0$ is $\pi_q(Da_!T_X)^{-1}\circ Rq_*\rho$. Naturality of the proper projection isomorphism [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] with respect to $u$ therefore gives
$$\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p,K_0}=(1_{K_0}\otimes t_q)\pi_q(T_P)^{-1}Rq_*(1\otimes u)Rq_*\rho
=(1_{K_0}\otimes\int_p)\pi_q(Da_!T_X)^{-1}Rq_*\rho.$$
This is precisely the projection-formula integration composite defining the comparison in [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison].

source.place: Proof, second sentence: calculate the actual composite counit as projection-formula integration

proof.text: Let $p^\times$ be the ordinary etale right adjoint supplied by [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] for the fixed compactification $(a,q)$. Compare $F_p\dashv G_p$ of Step 2 with $F_p\dashv p^\times$. Apply [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] to the identity isomorphism of their common left adjoint $F_p$. Its conjugate $\delta:G_p\xrightarrow{\sim}p^\times$ is a natural isomorphism, and its component $\delta_{K_0}$ is the transpose of $\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p,K_0}$ under $F_p\dashv p^\times$ (the formula for the conjugate is the unit followed by the image of this counit). Step 3 identifies that counit with integration. Consequently it is the specified comparison, rather than merely some isomorphism between the same two objects, that is invertible on the etale site. Naturality is also obtained here from the natural transformation $\delta$.

source.place: Proof, third sentence: uniqueness of right adjoints with the specified counit

u_Y^*F_pM$ for bounded-below $M$. The unit isomorphism of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] identifies $R
u_{Y,*}K$ with $K_0$ via the witness $\alpha$. Under these identifications [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] gives exactly the transported adjunction bijection with right adjoint $
u_X^*p^	imes R
u_{Y,*}$. The comparison inverse image is exact by [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]; its tensor comparison is the ringed-topos isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The inverse-image squares commute because the inclusions defining [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] commute with base change of etale schemes: both composites send a test scheme to its fibre product with the same scheme. With the comparison $	au_X:C_XB_X\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(1)$ of [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison], where $B_X$ is the ordinary etale twist of Step 2 (the twist identification used by [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison]; it commutes with inverse image), these give $
u_X^*G_pK_0\cong Lp^*K(1)[2]$. It remains to match the counit of Step 3 with the pro-etale composite $a_K$ of the definition, not merely its endpoints. [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison], applied over $S=Y$ to the trivial rank-one bundle $X	o Y$ with its global coordinate (as in the definition), gives exactly this: its projective-line clause says that $ eta_q$ and the comparison $C_Pj^e_!\cong j^p_!C_X$, which identifies the two extension-by-zero counits, carry the restricted etale trace $\int_p^e=t^e_q\circ Rq_*(u)$ of Step 3 to the restricted pro-etale trace $\int_p$ of the definition. Its projection clause says that the same comparisons identify the etale and pro-etale compact-support tensor projection maps on $K_0\in D^b_{ctf}(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Hence under the compact-support comparison $ eta_p:C_YF_p\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_!C_X$ (an isomorphism on these bounded-below witnessed inputs, also by [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]) and $\alpha$, $C_Y(\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p,K_0})$ is $a_K$. Its final clause states the transposed form: the pro-etale transpose of $a_{C_YK_0}$ is $C_X$ of the etale transpose. By Step 4 the etale transpose is $\delta_{K_0}$. Applying the transported Hom bijection therefore gives precisely $\gamma_{p,K}$ of [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison], as $
u_X^*\delta_{K_0}$ conjugated by the displayed endpoint isomorphisms. It is invertible and natural in $K$. Changing the witness changes both sides by these natural endpoint isomorphisms; full faithfulness makes the result independent of the witness. Its source is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude by Step 1, hence so is its isomorphic target. This uses only the bounded-below etale-origin adjunction, never an adjunction on all pro-etale complexes.

source.place: Proof, fourth and fifth sentences: realize the actual adjunction and its natural comparison

proof.text:
Check the orientation normalization. Let $D_0=s(Y)$, viewed also as the zero-section divisor in $P$. Its equations on the standard two affine charts are $t$ and $1$, so the dual ideal generators have transition $t^{-1}$; thus $\mathcal O_P(D_0)=\mathcal O_P(1)$ with the transition convention used in the projective-line class. This follows directly from [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle]. The supported Kummer morphism of [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] for this Cartier divisor, after forgetting supports, is therefore $h=c_1(\mathcal O_P(1))$. On $X$ it is the boundary of the coordinate $t$, and [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] identifies its finite-coefficient realization with the same supported morphism on the pro-etale site. This is the boundary defining $\operatorname{pur}_s$ in [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation]. The trace of [def-amb-p1-trace] satisfies $t_qh=1$. Hence $\int_p$ sends the image of this supported orientation to $1$. For the proper zero section, the identity-open compactification in [def-amb-etale-compact-support] gives $Rs_!=Rs_*$. The canonical composition of [thm-sf-comp-composition] and $ps=\mathrm{id}$ then give $Rp_!Rs_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ on these etale-origin inputs. Composing the two Hom bijections for the zero section and projection, using the composite-counit formula of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] and $ps=\mathrm{id}$, identifies this evaluation with
$$\Lambda_Y\xrightarrow{\operatorname{pur}_s}Rs^!\Lambda_X(1)[2]\xrightarrow{Rs^!\gamma_{p,\Lambda}}Rs^!Rp^!\Lambda_Y\cong\Lambda_Y.$$
It is the identity, which verifies the stated normalization without multiplying the comparison by an unspecified unit.

source.place: Statement, normalization by the orientation; original sk-prop-an Step 5(d): Kummer class of the zero-section divisor

proof.text:
Let $g:Y'\to Y$ be an arbitrary morphism in the chapter's fixed setting, and write $g_X:X'\to X$, $g_P:P'\to P$, $a',q',p'$ for the pulled-back compactification. Here $Y'$ is again a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, as required by the chapter setting; $g$ is any $k$-morphism between these schemes. No flatness, smoothness, or etaleness is required of $g$. For $L$ bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude on $Y_{\mathrm{et}}$, all arguments of the following exchange maps are bounded below. On these ordinary etale inputs let $C_p:g^*F_p\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{p'}g_X^*$ be the compact-support exchange and $\tau_L:g_X^*G_pL\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{p'}g^*L$ the pullback/twist identification. The isomorphy of $C_p$ on these bounded-below inputs is [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]; the open $a$ is quasi-compact because $P$ is Noetherian. Use the actual compactification formula in [def-cbc-exchange-map]: proper exchange for $q$, followed by open-extension exchange for $a$. The latter is the inverse of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], applied degreewise using [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. The trace and projective-line adjunction normalization commute with base change by [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction]. The root-of-unity twist comparison is [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The projection transformations commute with the proper exchange by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence]; the open evaluation commutes with pullback because its maps are the identity on the open and zero off it, as specified in [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. Substituting these identities into the explicit counit formula of Step 2 yields the typed equality
$$g^*\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p,L}=\epsilon^{\mathrm{exp}}_{p',g^*L}\circ F_{p'}(\tau_L)\circ C_{p,G_pL}.$$
In particular this checks compatibility of the actual integration counit, not only of the two functors up to isomorphism.

source.place: Proof, final base-change sentences: check the defining counit before taking mates

proof.text:
Take mates of the equality in Step 7. Use [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] to change from the explicit adjunctions to the actual exceptional adjunctions through $\delta,\delta'$. If $\beta^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,g}:g_X^*p^\times\to p'^\times g^*$ is the canonical mate of $C_p^{-1}:F_{p'}g_X^*\to g^*F_p$, it is explicitly (its argument $p^\times L$ is bounded below, since Step 4 identifies it with $G_pL$)
$$\beta^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,g,L}=p'^\times\!\bigl(g^*\epsilon^{\times}_{p,L}\circ C_{p,p^\times L}^{-1}\bigr)\circ\eta'_{g_X^*p^\times L},$$
where $\eta'$ is the unit of $F_{p'}\dashv p'^\times$ and $\epsilon^{\times}$ is the actual exceptional counit. Its defining counit equation gives
$$\beta^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,g,L}\circ g_X^*\delta_L=\delta'_{g^*L}\circ\tau_L.$$
Both sides have the same transpose by Step 7, so equality follows from the adjunction bijection. Now choose the witness $K_0$ of Step 1 and its pullback $g^*K_0$ as witness for $Lg^*K$. The exchange in [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] is explicitly the transport of this ordinary compact-support exchange. The Hom bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] and the unit isomorphism of [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] therefore identify its exceptional mate with the realization of $\beta^{\mathrm{et}}_{p,g,K_0}$. Applying $\nu_{X'}^*$ to the preceding equality and using the endpoint identifications of Step 5 over $Y$ and $Y'$ gives the following. Those identifications are compatible with $g$: the comparisons of [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] apply over the finite-type $k$-scheme $Y'$, and its twist maps $\tau_T$ commute with inverse image along $g_X$. The result is
$$\beta_{p,g,K}\circ Lg_X^*\gamma_{p,K}=\gamma_{p',Lg^*K}\circ\tau_K.$$
The terms involving $Lg^*K$ are defined in $D^b_{ctf}$ by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude]. The two purity comparisons are isomorphisms by Steps 1--5 applied over $Y$ and $Y'$, and $\tau_K$ is an isomorphism, so this equation also proves that the canonical exceptional base-change mate $\beta_{p,g,K}$ is invertible. This is the asserted arbitrary base-change compatibility.

In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting), let $Y$ be the scheme of the
affine-line datum and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$ with $\Lambda=A$. The affine-line purity
comparison $\gamma_{p,K}$ of
[def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison] – the adjoint of the
projection-formula composite
$Rp_!Lp^*K(1)[2]\cong K\otimes^L Rp_!\Lambda_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]\to K$
formed with the projective-line trace and normalized by the orientation
$\operatorname{pur}_s$ of [thm-pur-affine-line-orientation] – is an isomorphism

$$
\gamma_{p,K}:Lp^*K(1)[2]\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }Rp^!K.
$$

It is natural in $K$ and compatible with arbitrary base change of $Y$.

proof.text:
On the ordinary etale site, [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction]
constructs $Rp_!\dashv p^*(1)[2]$ by composing
$j_!\dashv j^*$ with the explicit projective-line adjunction.
Its counit is exactly the composite in
[def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison], since
[def-amb-p1-trace] defines the same normalized trace.
Uniqueness of a right adjoint with its counit therefore identifies its
adjoint $\gamma_{p,K}$ with an isomorphism.
The actual-adjoint comparison of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]
and [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] transport this statement and
the adjunction bijection to the finite etale-origin coefficients of
this chapter. Naturality follows from the defining adjunction.
For base change, [prop-asd-smooth-base-change] identifies the mate
of compact-support base change with the inverse-image and twist
identification for this explicit affine-line adjunction. Hence the
same defining counit, and therefore $\gamma_{p,K}$, commutes with
arbitrary base change. General smooth purity is not an input here.
